love.event.pump.description:
Pump events into the event queue.

This is a low-level function, and is usually not called by the user, but by love.run.

Note that this does need to be called for any OS to think you're still running,

and if you want to handle OS-generated events at all (think callbacks).

love.filesystem.isFused.description:
Gets whether the game is in fused mode or not.

If a game is in fused mode, its save directory will be directly in the Appdata directory instead of Appdata/LOVE/. The game will also be able to load C Lua dynamic libraries which are located in the save directory.

A game is in fused mode if the source .love has been fused to the executable (see Game Distribution), or if '--fused' has been given as a command-line argument when starting the game.

returns.name: fused
returns.description: True if the game is in fused mode, false otherwise.

love.filesystem.getRequirePath.description:
Gets the filesystem paths that will be searched when require is called.

The paths string returned by this function is a sequence of path templates separated by semicolons. The argument passed to ''require'' will be inserted in place of any question mark ('?') character in each template (after the dot characters in the argument passed to ''require'' are replaced by directory separators.)

The paths are relative to the game's source and save directories, as well as any paths mounted with love.filesystem.mount.

returns.name: paths
returns.description: The paths that the ''require'' function will check in love's filesystem.

love.filesystem.setRequirePath.description:
Sets the filesystem paths that will be searched when require is called.

The paths string given to this function is a sequence of path templates separated by semicolons. The argument passed to ''require'' will be inserted in place of any question mark ('?') character in each template (after the dot characters in the argument passed to ''require'' are replaced by directory separators.)

The paths are relative to the game's source and save directories, as well as any paths mounted with love.filesystem.mount.

params.name: paths
params.description: The paths that the ''require'' function will check in love's filesystem.

love.filesystem.getCRequirePath.description:
Gets the filesystem paths that will be searched for c libraries when require is called.

The paths string returned by this function is a sequence of path templates separated by semicolons. The argument passed to ''require'' will be inserted in place of any question mark ('?') character in each template (after the dot characters in the argument passed to ''require'' are replaced by directory separators.) Additionally, any occurrence of a double question mark ('??') will be replaced by the name passed to require and the default library extension for the platform.

The paths are relative to the game's source and save directories, as well as any paths mounted with love.filesystem.mount.

returns.name: paths
returns.description: The paths that the ''require'' function will check for c libraries in love's filesystem.

love.filesystem.setCRequirePath.description:
Sets the filesystem paths that will be searched for c libraries when require is called.

The paths string returned by this function is a sequence of path templates separated by semicolons. The argument passed to ''require'' will be inserted in place of any question mark ('?') character in each template (after the dot characters in the argument passed to ''require'' are replaced by directory separators.) Additionally, any occurrence of a double question mark ('??') will be replaced by the name passed to require and the default library extension for the platform.

The paths are relative to the game's source and save directories, as well as any paths mounted with love.filesystem.mount.

params.name: paths
params.description: The paths that the ''require'' function will check in love's filesystem.

love.graphics.reset.description:
Resets the current graphics settings.

Calling reset makes the current drawing color white, the current background color black, disables any active color component masks, disables wireframe mode and resets the current graphics transformation to the origin. It also sets both the point and line drawing modes to smooth and their sizes to 1.0.

love.graphics.clear.description:
Clears the screen or active Canvas to the specified color.

This function is called automatically before love.draw in the default love.run function. See the example in love.run for a typical use of this function.

Note that the scissor area bounds the cleared region.

In versions prior to 11.0, color component values were within the range of 0 to 255 instead of 0 to 1.

In versions prior to background color instead.

love.graphics.discard.description:
Discards (trashes) the contents of the screen or active Canvas. This is a performance optimization function with niche use cases.

If the active Canvas has just been changed and the 'replace' BlendMode is about to be used to draw something which covers the entire screen, calling love.graphics.discard rather than calling love.graphics.clear or doing nothing may improve performance on mobile devices.

On some desktop systems this function may do nothing.

params.name: discardcolor
params.description: Whether to discard the texture(s) of the active Canvas(es) (the contents of the screen if no Canvas is active.)

params.name: discardstencil
params.description: Whether to discard the contents of the stencil buffer of the screen / active Canvas.

love.graphics.present.description:
Displays the results of drawing operations on the screen.

This function is used when writing your own love.run function. It presents all the results of your drawing operations on the screen. See the example in love.run for a typical use of this function.

love.graphics.newCanvas.description: Creates a new Canvas object for offscreen rendering.

returns.name: canvas
returns.description: A new Canvas with dimensions equal to the window's size in pixels.

love.graphics.newQuad.description:
Creates a new Quad.

The purpose of a Quad is to use a fraction of an image to draw objects, as opposed to drawing entire image. It is most useful for sprite sheets and atlases: in a sprite atlas, multiple sprites reside in same image, quad is used to draw a specific sprite from that image; in animated sprites with all frames residing in the same image, quad is used to draw specific frame from the animation.

params.name: x
params.description: The top-left position in the Image along the x-axis.

params.name: y
params.description: The top-left position in the Image along the y-axis.

params.name: width
params.description: The width of the Quad in the Image. (Must be greater than 0.)

params.name: height
params.description: The height of the Quad in the Image. (Must be greater than 0.)

params.name: sw
params.description: The reference width, the width of the Image. (Must be greater than 0.)

params.name: sh
params.description: The reference height, the height of the Image. (Must be greater than 0.)

returns.name: quad
returns.description: The new Quad.

love.graphics.newFont.description:
Creates a new Font from a TrueType Font or BMFont file. Created fonts are not cached, in that calling this function with the same arguments will always create a new Font object.

All variants which accept a filename can also accept a Data object instead.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filepath to the BMFont or TrueType font file.

returns.name: font

Creates a new specifically formatted image.

In versions prior to 0.9.0, LÖVE expects ISO 8859-1 encoding for the glyphs string.

params.name: glyphs

returns.name: font

returns.name: spriteBatch
returns.description: The new SpriteBatch.

params.description: The image to use.

By default the coordinate system in LÖVE corresponds to the display pixels in horizontal and vertical directions one-to-one, and the x-axis increases towards the right while the y-axis increases downwards. Scaling the coordinate system changes this relation.

After scaling by sx and sy, all coordinates are treated as if they were multiplied by sx and sy. Every result of a drawing operation is also correspondingly scaled, so scaling by (2, 2) for example would mean making everything twice as large in both x- and y-directions. Scaling by a negative value flips the coordinate system in the corresponding direction, which also means everything…

params.name: sx
params.description: The scaling in the direction of the x-axis.

params.name: sy
params.description: The scaling in the direction of the y-axis. If omitted, it defaults to same as parameter sx.

love.graphics.translate.description:
Translates the coordinate system in two dimensions.

When this function is called with two numbers, dx, and dy, all the following drawing operations take effect as if their x and y coordinates were x+dx and y+dy.

Scale and translate are not commutative operations, therefore, calling them in different orders will change the outcome.

This change lasts until love.draw() exits or else a love.graphics.pop reverts to a previous love.graphics.push.

Translating using whole numbers will prevent tearing/blurring of images and fonts draw after translating.

params.name: dx
params.description: The translation relative to the x-axis.

params.name: dy
params.description: The translation relative to the y-axis.

params.name: kx
params.description: The shear factor on the x-axis.

params.name: ky
params.description: The shear factor on the y-axis.

love.graphics.origin.description:
Resets the current coordinate transformation.

This function is always used to reverse any previous calls to love.graphics.rotate, love.graphics.scale, love.graphics.shear or love.graphics.translate. It returns the current transformation state to its defaults.

love.graphics.applyTransform.description:
Applies the given Transform object to the current coordinate transformation.

This effectively multiplies the existing coordinate transformation's matrix with the Transform object's internal matrix to produce the new coordinate transformation.

params.name: transform
params.description: The Transform object to apply to the current graphics coordinate transform.

love.graphics.replaceTransform.description: Replaces the current coordinate transformation with the given Transform object.

params.name: transform
params.description: The Transform object to replace the current graphics coordinate transform with.

love.graphics.transformPoint.description:
Converts the given 2D position from global coordinates into screen-space.

This effectively applies the current graphics transformations to the given position. A similar Transform:transformPoint method exists for Transform objects.

params.name: globalX
params.description: The x component of the position in global coordinates.

params.name: globalY
params.description: The y component of the position in global coordinates.

returns.name: screenX
returns.description: The x component of the position with graphics transformations applied.

returns.name: screenY
returns.description: The y component of the position with graphics transformations applied.

love.graphics.inverseTransformPoint.description:
Converts the given 2D position from screen-space into global coordinates.

This effectively applies the reverse of the current graphics transformations to the given position. A similar Transform:inverseTransformPoint method exists for Transform objects.

params.name: screenX
params.description: The x component of the screen-space position.

params.name: screenY
params.description: The y component of the screen-space position.

returns.name: globalX
returns.description: The x component of the position in global coordinates.

returns.name: globalY
returns.description: The y component of the position in global coordinates.

love.graphics.newImage.description: Creates a new Image from a filepath, FileData, an ImageData, or a CompressedImageData, and optionally generates or specifies mipmaps for the image.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filepath to the image file.

params.name: settings
params.description: A table containing the following fields:

returns.name: image
returns.description: A new Image object which can be drawn on screen.

love.graphics.newArrayImage.description:
Creates a new array Image.

An array image / array texture is a single object which contains multiple 'layers' or 'slices' of 2D sub-images. It can be thought of similarly to a texture atlas or sprite sheet, but it doesn't suffer from the same tile / quad bleeding artifacts that texture atlases do – although every sub-image must have the same dimensions.

A specific layer of an array image can be drawn with love.graphics.drawLayer / SpriteBatch:addLayer, or with the Quad variant of love.graphics.draw and Quad:setLayer, or via a custom Shader.

To use an array image in a Shader, it must be declared as a ArrayImage or sampler2DArray type (instead of Image or sampler2D). The Texel(ArrayImage…

params.name: slices
params.description: A table containing filepaths to images (or File, FileData, ImageData, or CompressedImageData objects), in an array. Each sub-image must have the same dimensions. A table of tables can also be given, where each sub-table contains all mipmap levels for the slice index of that sub-table.

params.name: settings
params.description: Optional table of settings to configure the array image, containing the following fields:

returns.name: image
returns.description: An Array Image object.

love.graphics.newVolumeImage.description:
Creates a new volume (3D) Image.

Volume images are 3D textures with width, height, and depth. They can't be rendered directly, they can only be used in Shader code (and sent to the shader via Shader:send).

To use a volume image in a Shader, it must be declared as a VolumeImage or sampler3D type (instead of Image or sampler2D). The Texel(VolumeImage image, vec3 texcoords) shader function must be used to get pixel colors from the volume image. The vec3 argument is a normalized texture coordinate with the z component representing the depth to sample at (ranging from 1).

Volume images are typically used as lookup tables in shaders for color grading, for example, because sampling using a…

params.name: layers
params.description: A table containing filepaths to images (or File, FileData, ImageData, or CompressedImageData objects), in an array. A table of tables can also be given, where each sub-table represents a single mipmap level and contains all layers for that mipmap.

params.name: settings
params.description: Optional table of settings to configure the volume image, containing the following fields:

returns.name: image
returns.description: A volume Image object.

love.graphics.newCubeImage.description:
Creates a new cubemap Image.

Cubemap images have 6 faces (sides) which represent a cube. They can't be rendered directly, they can only be used in Shader code (and sent to the shader via Shader:send).

To use a cubemap image in a Shader, it must be declared as a CubeImage or samplerCube type (instead of Image or sampler2D). The Texel(CubeImage image, vec3 direction) shader function must be used to get pixel colors from the cubemap. The vec3 argument is a normalized direction from the center of the cube, rather than explicit texture coordinates.

Each face in a cubemap image must have square dimensions.

For variants of this function which accept a single image containing multiple cubemap…

params.name: filename
params.description: The filepath to a cubemap image file (or a File, FileData, or ImageData).

params.name: settings
params.description: Optional table of settings to configure the cubemap image, containing the following fields:

returns.name: image
returns.description: An cubemap Image object.

love.graphics.newText.description: Creates a new drawable Text object.

params.name: font
params.description: The font to use for the text.

params.name: textstring
params.description: The initial string of text that the new Text object will contain. May be nil.

returns.name: text
returns.description: The new drawable Text object.

love.graphics.getCanvasFormats.description: Gets the available Canvas formats, and whether each is supported.

returns.name: formats
returns.description: A table containing CanvasFormats as keys, and a boolean indicating whether the format is supported as values. Not all systems support all formats.

love.graphics.getImageFormats.description: Gets the raw and compressed pixel formats usable for Images, and whether each is supported.

returns.name: formats
returns.description: A table containing PixelFormats as keys, and a boolean indicating whether the format is supported as values. Not all systems support all formats.

params.name: width
params.description: The width of the ImageData.

params.name: height
params.description: The height of the ImageData.

returns.name: imageData
returns.description: The new blank ImageData object. Each pixel's color values, (including the alpha values!) will be set to zero.

love.image.newCompressedData.description: Create a new CompressedImageData object from a compressed image file. LÖVE supports several compressed texture formats, enumerated in the CompressedImageFormat page.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filename of the compressed image file.

returns.name: compressedImageData
returns.description: The new CompressedImageData object.

love.image.isCompressed.description: Determines whether a file can be loaded as CompressedImageData.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filename of the potentially compressed image file.

returns.name: compressed
returns.description: Whether the file can be loaded as CompressedImageData or not.

love.joystick.getJoysticks.description: Gets a list of connected Joysticks.

returns.name: joysticks
returns.description: The list of currently connected Joysticks.

love.joystick.getJoystickCount.description: Gets the number of connected joysticks.

returns.name: joystickcount
returns.description: The number of connected joysticks.

love.joystick.setGamepadMapping.description:
Binds a virtual gamepad input to a button, axis or hat for all Joysticks of a certain type. For example, if this function is used with a GUID returned by a Dualshock 3 controller in OS X, the binding will affect Joystick:getGamepadAxis and Joystick:isGamepadDown for ''all'' Dualshock 3 controllers used with the game when run in OS X.

LÖVE includes built-in gamepad bindings for many common controllers. This function lets you change the bindings or add new ones for types of Joysticks which aren't recognized as gamepads by default.

The virtual gamepad buttons and axes are designed around the Xbox 360 controller layout.

params.name: guid
params.description: The OS-dependent GUID for the type of Joystick the binding will affect.

params.name: button
params.description: The virtual gamepad button to bind.

params.name: inputtype
params.description: The type of input to bind the virtual gamepad button to.

params.name: inputindex
params.description: The index of the axis, button, or hat to bind the virtual gamepad button to.

params.name: hatdir
params.description: The direction of the hat, if the virtual gamepad button will be bound to a hat. nil otherwise.

returns.name: success
returns.description: Whether the virtual gamepad button was successfully bound.

love.joystick.loadGamepadMappings.description:
Loads a gamepad mappings string or file created with love.joystick.saveGamepadMappings.

It also recognizes any SDL gamecontroller mapping string, such as those created with Steam's Big Picture controller configure interface, or this nice database. If a new mapping is loaded for an already known controller GUID, the later version will overwrite the one currently loaded.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filename to load the mappings string from.

love.joystick.saveGamepadMappings.description:
Saves the virtual gamepad mappings of all recognized as gamepads and have either been recently used or their gamepad bindings have been modified.

The mappings are stored as a string for use with love.joystick.loadGamepadMappings.

params.name: filename
params.description: The filename to save the mappings string to.

returns.name: mappings
returns.description: The mappings string that was written to the file.

love.joystick.getGamepadMappingString.description:
Gets the full gamepad mapping string of the Joysticks which have the given GUID, or nil if the GUID isn't recognized as a gamepad.

The mapping string contains binding information used to map the Joystick's buttons an axes to the standard gamepad layout, and can be used later with love.joystick.loadGamepadMappings.

params.name: guid
params.description: The GUID value to get the mapping string for.

returns.name: mappingstring
returns.description: A string containing the Joystick's gamepad mappings, or nil if the GUID is not recognized as a gamepad.

love.keyboard.setKeyRepeat.description: Enables or disables key repeat for love.keypressed. It is disabled by default.

params.name: enable
params.description: Whether repeat keypress events should be enabled when a key is held down.

love.keyboard.hasKeyRepeat.description: Gets whether key repeat is enabled.

returns.name: enabled
returns.description: Whether key repeat is enabled.

love.keyboard.setTextInput.description:
Enables or disables text input events. It is enabled by default on Windows, Mac, and Linux, and disabled by default on iOS and Android.

On touch devices, this shows the system's native on-screen keyboard when it's enabled.

params.name: enable
params.description: Whether text input events should be enabled.

love.keyboard.hasTextInput.description: Gets whether text input events are enabled.

returns.name: enabled
returns.description: Whether text input events are enabled.

love.keyboard.hasScreenKeyboard.description: Gets whether screen keyboard is supported.

returns.name: supported
returns.description: Whether screen keyboard is supported.

love.keyboard.isDown.description: Checks whether a certain key is down. Not to be confused with love.keypressed or love.keyreleased.

params.name: key
params.description: The key to check.

returns.name: down
returns.description: True if the key is down, false if not.

love.keyboard.isScancodeDown.description:
Checks whether the specified Scancodes are pressed. Not to be confused with love.keypressed or love.keyreleased.

Unlike regular KeyConstants, Scancodes are keyboard layout-independent. The scancode 'w' is used if the key in the same place as the 'w' key on an American keyboard is pressed, no matter what the key is labelled or what the user's operating system settings are.

params.name: scancode
params.description: A Scancode to check.

returns.name: down
returns.description: True if any supplied Scancode is down, false if not.

love.keyboard.getScancodeFromKey.description:
Gets the hardware scancode corresponding to the given key.

Unlike key constants, Scancodes are keyboard layout-independent. For example the scancode 'w' will be generated if the key in the same place as the 'w' key on an American keyboard is pressed, no matter what the key is labelled or what the user's operating system settings are.

Scancodes are useful for creating default controls that have the same physical locations on on all systems.

params.name: key
params.description: The key to get the scancode from.

returns.name: scancode
returns.description: The scancode corresponding to the given key, or 'unknown' if the given key has no known physical representation on the current system.

love.keyboard.getKeyFromScancode.description:
Gets the key corresponding to the given hardware scancode.

Unlike key constants, Scancodes are keyboard layout-independent. For example the scancode 'w' will be generated if the key in the same place as the 'w' key on an American keyboard is pressed, no matter what the key is labelled or what the user's operating system settings are.

Scancodes are useful for creating default controls that have the same physical locations on on all systems.

params.name: scancode
params.description: The scancode to get the key from.

returns.name: key
returns.description: The key corresponding to the given scancode, or 'unknown' if the scancode doesn't map to a KeyConstant on the current system.

love.math.newRandomGenerator.description: Creates a new RandomGenerator object which is completely independent of other RandomGenerator objects and random functions.

returns.name: rng
returns.description: The new Random Number Generator object.

love.math.newBezierCurve.description:
Creates a new BezierCurve object.

The number of vertices in the control polygon determines the degree of the curve, e.g. three vertices define a quadratic (degree 2) Bézier curve, four vertices define a cubic (degree 3) Bézier curve, etc.

params.name: vertices
params.description: The vertices of the control polygon as a table in the form of {x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, ...}.

returns.name: curve
returns.description: A Bézier curve object.

returns.name: transform
returns.description: The new Transform object.

love.math.triangulate.description: Decomposes a simple convex or concave polygon into triangles.

params.name: polygon
params.description: Polygon to triangulate. Must not intersect itself.

returns.name: triangles
returns.description: List of triangles the polygon is composed of, in the form of {{x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3},  {x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3}, ...}.

love.math.isConvex.description:
Checks whether a polygon is convex.

PolygonShapes in love.physics, some forms of Meshes, and polygons drawn with love.graphics.polygon must be simple convex polygons.

params.name: vertices
params.description: The vertices of the polygon as a table in the form of {x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, ...}.

returns.name: convex
returns.description: Whether the given polygon is convex.

love.math.gammaToLinear.description:
Converts a color from gamma-space (sRGB) to linear-space (RGB). This is useful when doing gamma-correct rendering and you need to do math in linear RGB in the few cases where LÖVE doesn't handle conversions automatically.

Read more about gamma-correct rendering here, here, and here.

In versions prior to 11.0, color component values were within the range of 0 to 255 instead of 0 to 1.

params.name: r
params.description: The red channel of the sRGB color to convert.

params.name: g
params.description: The green channel of the sRGB color to convert.

params.name: b
params.description: The blue channel of the sRGB color to convert.

returns.name: lr
returns.description: The red channel of the converted color in linear RGB space.

returns.name: lg
returns.description: The green channel of the converted color in linear RGB space.

returns.name: lb
returns.description: The blue channel of the converted color in linear RGB space.

love.math.linearToGamma.description:
Converts a color from linear-space (RGB) to gamma-space (sRGB). This is useful when storing linear RGB color values in an image, because the linear RGB color space has less precision than sRGB for dark colors, which can result in noticeable color banding when drawing.

In general, colors chosen based on what they look like on-screen are already in gamma-space and should not be double-converted. Colors calculated using math are often in the linear RGB space.

Read more about gamma-correct rendering here, here, and here.

In versions prior to 11.0, color component values were within the range of 0 to 255 instead of 0 to 1.

params.name: lr
params.description: The red channel of the linear RGB color to convert.

params.name: lg
params.description: The green channel of the linear RGB color to convert.

params.name: lb
params.description: The blue channel of the linear RGB color to convert.

returns.name: cr
returns.description: The red channel of the converted color in gamma sRGB space.

returns.name: cg
returns.description: The green channel of the converted color in gamma sRGB space.

returns.name: cb
returns.description: The blue channel of the converted color in gamma sRGB space.

love.math.noise.description:
Generates a Simplex or Perlin noise value in 1-4 dimensions. The return value will always be the same, given the same arguments.

Simplex noise is closely related to Perlin noise. It is widely used for procedural content generation.

There are many webpages which discuss Perlin and Simplex noise in detail.

params.name: x
params.description: The number used to generate the noise value.

returns.name: value
returns.description: The noise value in the range of 1.

love.mouse.newCursor.description:
Creates a new hardware Cursor object from an image file or ImageData.

Hardware cursors are framerate-independent and work the same way as normal operating system cursors. Unlike drawing an image at the mouse's current coordinates, hardware cursors never have visible lag between when the mouse is moved and when the cursor position updates, even at low framerates.

The hot spot is the point the operating system uses to determine what was clicked and at what position the mouse cursor is. For example, the normal arrow pointer normally has its hot spot at the top left of the image, but a crosshair cursor might have it in the middle.

params.name: imageData
params.description: The ImageData to use for the new Cursor.

params.name: hotx
params.description: The x-coordinate in the ImageData of the cursor's hot spot.

params.name: hoty
params.description: The y-coordinate in the ImageData of the cursor's hot spot.

returns.name: cursor
returns.description: The new Cursor object.

love.mouse.getSystemCursor.description:
Gets a Cursor object representing a system-native hardware cursor.

Hardware cursors are framerate-independent and work the same way as normal operating system cursors. Unlike drawing an image at the mouse's current coordinates, hardware cursors never have visible lag between when the mouse is moved and when the cursor position updates, even at low framerates.

params.name: ctype
params.description: The type of system cursor to get.

returns.name: cursor
returns.description: The Cursor object representing the system cursor type.

params.name: cursor
params.description: The Cursor object to use as the current mouse cursor.

returns.name: cursor
returns.description: The current cursor, or nil if no cursor is set.

love.mouse.isCursorSupported.description:
Gets whether cursor functionality is supported.

If it isn't supported, calling love.mouse.newCursor and love.mouse.getSystemCursor will cause an error. Mobile devices do not support cursors.

returns.name: supported
returns.description: Whether the system has cursor functionality.

love.mouse.getX.description: Returns the current x-position of the mouse.

returns.name: x
returns.description: The position of the mouse along the x-axis.

love.mouse.getY.description: Returns the current y-position of the mouse.

returns.name: y
returns.description: The position of the mouse along the y-axis.

love.mouse.setX.description:
Sets the current X position of the mouse.

Non-integer values are floored.

params.name: x
params.description: The new position of the mouse along the x-axis.

love.mouse.setY.description:
Sets the current Y position of the mouse.

Non-integer values are floored.

params.name: y
params.description: The new position of the mouse along the y-axis.

love.mouse.setPosition.description: Sets the current position of the mouse. Non-integer values are floored.

params.name: x
params.description: The new position of the mouse along the x-axis.

params.name: y
params.description: The new position of the mouse along the y-axis.

love.mouse.isDown.description:
Checks whether a certain mouse button is down.

This function does not detect mouse wheel scrolling; you must use the love.wheelmoved (or love.mousepressed in version 0.9.2 and older) callback for that.

params.name: button
params.description: The index of a button to check. 1 is the primary mouse button, 2 is the secondary mouse button and 3 is the middle button. Further buttons are mouse dependant.

returns.name: down
returns.description: True if any specified button is down.

love.mouse.setVisible.description: Sets the current visibility of the cursor.

params.name: visible
params.description: True to set the cursor to visible, false to hide the cursor.

love.mouse.isVisible.description: Checks if the cursor is visible.

returns.name: visible
returns.description: True if the cursor to visible, false if the cursor is hidden.

love.mouse.getPosition.description: Returns the current position of the mouse.

returns.name: x
returns.description: The position of the mouse along the x-axis.

returns.name: y
returns.description: The position of the mouse along the y-axis.

love.mouse.setGrabbed.description: Grabs the mouse and confines it to the window.

params.name: grab
params.description: True to confine the mouse, false to let it leave the window.

love.mouse.isGrabbed.description: Checks if the mouse is grabbed.

returns.name: grabbed
returns.description: True if the cursor is grabbed, false if it is not.

love.mouse.setRelativeMode.description:
Sets whether relative mode is enabled for the mouse.

When relative mode is enabled, the cursor is hidden and doesn't move when the mouse does, but relative mouse motion events are still generated via love.mousemoved. This lets the mouse move in any direction indefinitely without the cursor getting stuck at the edges of the screen.

The reported position of the mouse may not be updated while relative mode is enabled, even when relative mouse motion events are generated.

params.name: enable
params.description: True to enable relative mode, false to disable it.

love.mouse.getRelativeMode.description:
Gets whether relative mode is enabled for the mouse.

If relative mode is enabled, the cursor is hidden and doesn't move when the mouse does, but relative mouse motion events are still generated via love.mousemoved. This lets the mouse move in any direction indefinitely without the cursor getting stuck at the edges of the screen.

The reported position of the mouse is not updated while relative mode is enabled, even when relative mouse motion events are generated.

returns.name: enabled
returns.description: True if relative mode is enabled, false if it's disabled.

params.name: xg
params.description: The x component of gravity.

params.name: yg
params.description: The y component of gravity.

params.name: sleep
params.description: Whether the bodies in this world are allowed to sleep.

returns.description: A brave new World.

love.physics.newBody.description:
Creates a new body.

There are three types of bodies.

* Static bodies do not move, have a infinite mass, and can be used for level boundaries.

* Dynamic bodies are the main actors in the simulation, they collide with everything.

* Kinematic bodies do not react to forces and only collide with dynamic bodies.

The mass of the body gets calculated when a Fixture is attached or removed, but can be changed at any time with Body:setMass or Body:resetMassData.

params.name: world
params.description: The world to create the body in.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position of the body.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position of the body.

params.name: type
params.description: The type of the body.

returns.name: body
returns.description: A new body.

params.name: radius
params.description: The radius of the circle.

returns.name: shape
returns.description: The new shape.

love.physics.newRectangleShape.description:
Shorthand for creating rectangular PolygonShapes.

By default, the local origin is located at the '''center''' of the rectangle as opposed to the top left for graphics.

params.name: width

params.name: height

love.physics.newPolygonShape.description:
Creates a new PolygonShape.

This shape can have 8 vertices at most, and must form a convex shape.

params.name: y1

params.name: y1
params.description: The y position of the first point.

params.description: The y position of the second point.

returns.name: shape

returns.description: The new shape.

love.physics.newDistanceJoint.description:
Creates a DistanceJoint between two bodies.

This joint constrains the distance between two points on two bodies to be constant. These two points are specified in world coordinates and the two bodies are assumed to be in place when this joint is created. The first anchor point is connected to the first body and the second to the second body, and the points define the length of the distance joint.

params.name: body1
params.description: The first body to attach to the joint.

params.name: body2
params.description: The second body to attach to the joint.

params.name: x1
params.description: The x position of the first anchor point (world space).

params.name: y1
params.description: The y position of the first anchor point (world space).

params.name: x2
params.description: The x position of the second anchor point (world space).

params.name: y2
params.description: The y position of the second anchor point (world space).

params.name: collideConnected
params.description: Specifies whether the two bodies should collide with each other.

returns.name: joint
returns.description: The new distance joint.

love.physics.newMouseJoint.description:
Create a joint between a body and the mouse.

This joint actually connects the body to a fixed point in the world. To make it follow the mouse, the fixed point must be updated every timestep (example below).

The advantage of using a MouseJoint instead of just changing a body position directly is that collisions and reactions to other joints are handled by the physics engine.

params.name: body
params.description: The body to attach to the mouse.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position of the connecting point.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position of the connecting point.

returns.name: joint
returns.description: The new mouse joint.

love.physics.newRevoluteJoint.description:
Creates a pivot joint between two bodies.

This joint connects two bodies to a point around which they can pivot.

params.name: body1
params.description: The first body.

params.name: body2
params.description: The second body.

params.name: x
params.description: The x position of the connecting point.

params.name: y
params.description: The y position of the connecting point.

params.name: collideConnected
params.description: Specifies whether the two bodies should collide with each other.

returns.name: joint

love.physics.newPrismaticJoint.description:
Creates a PrismaticJoint between two bodies.

A prismatic joint constrains two bodies to move relatively to each other on a specified axis. It does not allow for relative rotation. Its definition and operation are similar to a  revolute joint, but with translation and force substituted for angle and torque.

love.physics.newPulleyJoint.description:
Creates a PulleyJoint to join two bodies to each other and the ground.

The pulley joint simulates a pulley with an optional block and tackle. If the ratio parameter has a value different from one, then the simulated rope extends faster on one side than the other. In a pulley joint the total length of the simulated rope is the constant length1 + ratio * length2, which is set when the pulley joint is created.

Pulley joints can behave unpredictably if one side is fully extended. It is recommended that the method  setMaxLengths  be used to constrain the maximum lengths each side can attain.

love.physics.newGearJoint.description:
Create a GearJoint connecting two Joints.

The gear joint connects two joints that must be either  prismatic or  revolute joints. Using this joint requires that the joints it uses connect their respective bodies to the ground and have the ground as the first body. When destroying the bodies and joints you must make sure you destroy the gear joint before the other joints.

The gear joint has a ratio the determines how the angular or distance values of the connected joints relate to each other. The formula coordinate1 + ratio * coordinate2 always has a constant value that is set when the gear joint is created.

params.name: joint1

params.name: joint2

params.name: collideConnected

love.physics.newMotorJoint.description:
Creates a joint between two bodies which controls the relative motion between them.

Position and rotation offsets can be specified once the MotorJoint has been created, as well as the maximum motor force and torque that will be be applied to reach the target offsets.

love.physics.getDistance.description: Returns the two closest points between two fixtures and their distance.

params.name: fixture1

returns.name: distance

returns.description: The y-coordinate of the second point.

love.physics.getMeter.description:
Returns the meter scale factor.

All coordinates in the physics module are divided by this number, creating a convenient way to draw the objects directly to the screen without the need for graphics transformations.

It is recommended to create shapes no larger than 10 times the scale. This is important because Box2D is tuned to work well with shape sizes from 0.1 to 10 meters.

returns.name: scale
returns.description: The scale factor as an integer.

love.physics.setMeter.description:
Sets the pixels to meter scale factor.

All coordinates in the physics module are divided by this number and converted to meters, and it creates a convenient way to draw the objects directly to the screen without the need for graphics transformations.

It is recommended to create shapes no larger than 10 times the scale. This is important because Box2D is tuned to work well with shape sizes from 0.1 to 10 meters. The default meter scale is 30.

params.name: scale
params.description: The scale factor as an integer.

love.physics.newFixture.description:
Creates and attaches a Fixture to a body.

Note that the Shape object is copied rather than kept as a reference when the Fixture is created. To get the Shape object that the Fixture owns, use Fixture:getShape.

params.name: body
params.description: The body which gets the fixture attached.

params.name: shape
params.description: The shape to be copied to the fixture.

params.name: density
params.description: The density of the fixture.

returns.name: fixture

love.sound.newDecoder.description: Attempts to find a decoder for the encoded sound data in the specified file.

params.name: file
params.description: The file with encoded sound data.

params.name: buffer
params.description: The size of each decoded chunk, in bytes.

returns.name: decoder
returns.description: A new Decoder object.

love.sound.newSoundData.description:
Creates new SoundData from a filepath, File, or Decoder. It's also possible to create SoundData with a custom sample rate, channel and bit depth.

The sound data will be decoded to the memory in a raw format. It is recommended to create only short sounds like effects, as a 3 minute song uses 30 MB of memory this way.

params.name: filename

returns.name: soundData
returns.description: A new SoundData object.

love.system.getOS.description: Gets the current operating system. In general, LÖVE abstracts away the need to know the current operating system, but there are a few cases where it can be useful (especially in combination with os.execute.)

returns.name: osString
returns.description: The current operating system. 'OS X', 'Windows', 'Linux', 'Android' or 'iOS'.

love.system.getProcessorCount.description: Gets the amount of logical processor in the system.

returns.name: processorCount
returns.description: Amount of logical processors.

params.name: text
params.description: The new text to hold in the system's clipboard.

returns.name: text

love.system.getPowerInfo.description: Gets information about the system's power supply.

returns.name: state

love.system.openURL.description: Opens a URL with the user's web or file browser.

params.name: url

returns.name: success

love.system.vibrate.description: Causes the device to vibrate, if possible. Currently this will only work on Android and iOS devices that have a built-in vibration motor.

params.name: seconds
params.description: The duration to vibrate for. If called on an iOS device, it will always vibrate for 0.5 seconds due to limitations in the iOS system APIs.

love.system.hasBackgroundMusic.description:
Gets whether another application on the system is playing music in the background.

Currently this is implemented on iOS and Android, and will always return false on other operating systems. The t.audio.mixwithsystem flag in love.conf can be used to configure whether background audio / music from other apps should play while LÖVE is open.

returns.name: backgroundmusic
returns.description: True if the user is playing music in the background via another app, false otherwise.

love.thread.newThread.description: Creates a new Thread from a filename, string or FileData object containing Lua code.

params.name: filename
params.description: The name of the Lua file to use as the source.

returns.name: thread
returns.description: A new Thread that has yet to be started.

love.thread.newChannel.description:
Create a new unnamed thread channel.

One use for them is to pass new unnamed channels to other threads via Channel:push on a named channel.

returns.name: channel

params.name: name

love.timer.step.description:
Measures the time between two frames.

Calling this changes the return value of love.timer.getDelta.

love.timer.getDelta.description: Returns the time between the last two frames.

love.timer.getAverageDelta.description: Returns the average delta time (seconds per frame) over the last second.

Returns the value of a timer with an unspecified starting time.

This function should only be used to calculate differences between points in time, as the starting time of the timer is unknown.

returns.name: time

love.touch.getTouches.description: Gets a list of all active touch-presses.

love.window.setMode.description:
Sets the display mode and properties of the window.

If width or height is 0, setMode will use the width and height of the desktop.

love.window.setDisplaySleepEnabled.description:
Sets whether the display is allowed to sleep while the program is running.

The window is considered visible if it's not minimized and the program isn't hidden.

returns.description: True if the window is visible or false if not.

love.window.getDPIScale.description:
Gets the DPI scale factor associated with the window.

The pixel density inside the window might be greater (or smaller) than the 'size' of the window. For example on a retina screen in Mac OS X with the highdpi window flag enabled, the window may take up the same physical size as an 800x600 window, but the area inside the window uses 1600x1200 pixels. love.window.getDPIScale() would return 2.0 in that case.

The love.window.fromPixels and love.window.toPixels functions can also be used to convert between units.

The highdpi window flag must be enabled to use the full pixel density of a Retina screen on Mac OS X and iOS. The flag currently does nothing on Windows and Linux, and on Android…

Converts a number from density-independent units to pixels.

The pixel density inside the window might be greater (or smaller) than the 'size' of the window. For example on a retina screen in Mac OS X with the highdpi window flag enabled, the window may take up the same physical size as an 800x600 window, but the area inside the window uses 1600x1200 pixels. love.window.toPixels(800) would return 1600 in that case.

This is used to convert coordinates from the size users are expecting them to display at onscreen to pixels. love.window.fromPixels does the opposite. The highdpi window flag must be enabled to use the full pixel density of a Retina screen on Mac OS X and iOS. The flag currently…

love.window.fromPixels.description:

This function converts coordinates from pixels to the size users are expecting them to display at onscreen. love.window.toPixels does the opposite. The highdpi window flag must be enabled to use the full pixel density of a Retina screen on Mac OS X and iOS. The flag currently…

params.name: pixelvalue

love.window.minimize.description: Minimizes the window to the system's task bar / dock.

Makes the window as large as possible.

love.window.requestAttention.description:

love.getVersion.description: Gets the current running version of LÖVE.

You can use this file to overwrite the love.conf function, which is later called by the LÖVE 'boot' script. Using the love.conf function, you can set some configuration options, and change things like the default size of the window, which modules are loaded, and other stuff.

Source.description:
A Source represents audio you can play back.

You can do interesting things with Sources, like set the volume, pitch, and its position relative to the listener. Please note that positional audio only works for mono (i.e. non-stereo) sources.

The Source controls (play/pause/stop) act according to the following state table.

clone.description:
Creates an identical copy of the Source in the stopped state.

Static Sources will use significantly less memory and take much less time to be created if Source:clone is used to create them instead of love.audio.newSource, so this method should be preferred when making multiple Sources which play the same sound.

returns.name: source
returns.description: The new identical copy of this Source.

returns.name: success
returns.description: Whether the Source was able to successfully start playing.

setPitch.description: Sets the pitch of the Source.

params.name: pitch
params.description: Calculated with regard to 1 being the base pitch. Each reduction by 50 percent equals a pitch shift of -12 semitones (one octave reduction). Each doubling equals a pitch shift of 12 semitones (one octave increase). Zero is not a legal value.

getPitch.description: Gets the current pitch of the Source.

returns.name: pitch
returns.description: The pitch, where 1.0 is normal.

setVolume.description: Sets the current volume of the Source.

params.name: volume
params.description: The volume for a Source, where 1.0 is normal volume. Volume cannot be raised above 1.0.

getVolume.description: Gets the current volume of the Source.

returns.name: volume
returns.description: The volume of the Source, where 1.0 is normal volume.

seek.description: Sets the currently playing position of the Source.

params.name: offset
params.description: The position to seek to.

params.name: unit
params.description: The unit of the position value.

tell.description: Gets the currently playing position of the Source.

params.name: unit
params.description: The type of unit for the return value.

returns.name: position
returns.description: The currently playing position of the Source.

getDuration.description: Gets the duration of the Source. For streaming Sources it may not always be sample-accurate, and may return -1 if the duration cannot be determined at all.

params.name: unit
params.description: The time unit for the return value.

returns.name: duration
returns.description: The duration of the Source, or -1 if it cannot be determined.

setPosition.description: Sets the position of the Source. Please note that this only works for mono (i.e. non-stereo) sound files!

Sets the velocity of the Source.

This does '''not''' change the position of the Source, but lets the application know how it has to calculate the doppler effect.

params.name: y
params.description: The Y part of the velocity vector.

setCone.description: Sets the Source's directional volume cones. Together with Source:setDirection, the cone angles allow for the Source's volume to vary depending on its direction.

params.name: innerAngle
params.description: The inner angle from the Source's direction, in radians. The Source will play at normal volume if the listener is inside the cone defined by this angle.

params.name: outerAngle
params.description: The outer angle from the Source's direction, in radians. The Source will play at a volume between the normal and outer volumes, if the listener is in between the cones defined by the inner and outer angles.

params.name: outerVolume
params.description: The Source's volume when the listener is outside both the inner and outer cone angles.

getCone.description: Gets the Source's directional volume cones. Together with Source:setDirection, the cone angles allow for the Source's volume to vary depending on its direction.

returns.name: innerAngle
returns.description: The inner angle from the Source's direction, in radians. The Source will play at normal volume if the listener is inside the cone defined by this angle.

returns.name: outerAngle
returns.description: The outer angle from the Source's direction, in radians. The Source will play at a volume between the normal and outer volumes, if the listener is in between the cones defined by the inner and outer angles.

returns.name: outerVolume
returns.description: The Source's volume when the listener is outside both the inner and outer cone angles.

setRelative.description:
Sets whether the Source's position, velocity, direction, and cone angles are relative to the listener, or absolute.

By default, all sources are absolute and therefore relative to the origin of love's coordinate system 0, 0. Only absolute sources are affected by the position of the listener. Please note that positional audio only works for mono (i.e. non-stereo) sources.

params.name: enable
params.description: True to make the position, velocity, direction and cone angles relative to the listener, false to make them absolute.

isRelative.description: Gets whether the Source's position, velocity, direction, and cone angles are relative to the listener.

setAttenuationDistances.description:
Sets the reference and maximum attenuation distances of the Source. The parameters, combined with the current DistanceModel, affect how the Source's volume attenuates based on distance.

Distance attenuation is only applicable to Sources based on mono (rather than stereo) audio.

params.name: ref
params.description: The new reference attenuation distance. If the current DistanceModel is clamped, this is the minimum attenuation distance.

params.name: max
params.description: The new maximum attenuation distance.

getAttenuationDistances.description: Gets the reference and maximum attenuation distances of the Source. The values, combined with the current DistanceModel, affect how the Source's volume attenuates based on distance from the listener.

returns.name: ref
returns.description: The current reference attenuation distance. If the current DistanceModel is clamped, this is the minimum distance before the Source is no longer attenuated.

returns.name: max
returns.description: The current maximum attenuation distance.

setRolloff.description:
Sets the rolloff factor which affects the strength of the used distance attenuation.

Extended information and detailed formulas can be found in the chapter '3.4. Attenuation By Distance' of OpenAL 1.1 specification.

params.name: rolloff
params.description: The new rolloff factor.

getRolloff.description: Returns the rolloff factor of the source.

returns.name: rolloff
returns.description: The rolloff factor.

setAirAbsorption.description:
Sets the amount of air absorption applied to the Source.

By default the value is set to 0 which means that air absorption effects are disabled. A value of 1 will apply high frequency attenuation to the Source at a rate of 0.05 dB per meter.

Air absorption can simulate sound transmission through foggy air, dry air, smoky atmosphere, etc. It can be used to simulate different atmospheric conditions within different locations in an area.

params.description: The amount of air absorption applied to the Source. Must be between 0 and 10.

getAirAbsorption.description:

By default the value is set to 0 which means that air absorption effects are disabled. A value of 1 will apply high frequency attenuation to the Source at a rate of 0.05 dB per meter.

returns.name: amount
returns.description: The amount of air absorption applied to the Source.

Font.description: Defines the shape of characters that can be drawn onto the screen.

getHeight.description:
Gets the height of the Font.

The height of the font is the size including any spacing; the height which it will need.

params.name: text
params.description: A string.

returns.name: width
returns.description: The width of the text.

getWrap.description:
Gets formatting information for text, given a wrap limit.

This function accounts for newlines correctly (i.e. '\n').

params.name: text

returns.name: width

returns.name: wrappedtext

setLineHeight.description:
Sets the line height.

When rendering the font in lines the actual height will be determined by the line height multiplied by the height of the font. The default is 1.0.

params.name: height
params.description: The new line height.

getLineHeight.description:
Gets the line height.

This will be the value previously set by Font:setLineHeight, or 1.0 by default.

returns.name: height
returns.description: The current line height.

setFilter.description: Sets the filter mode for a font.

params.name: min

params.name: mag

params.name: anisotropy
params.description: Maximum amount of anisotropic filtering used.

returns.name: mag
returns.description: Filter mode used when magnifying the font.

getAscent.description:
Gets the ascent of the Font.

The ascent spans the distance between the baseline and the top of the glyph that reaches farthest from the baseline.

returns.name: ascent
returns.description: The ascent of the Font in pixels.

getDescent.description:
Gets the descent of the Font.

The descent spans the distance between the baseline and the lowest descending glyph in a typeface.

returns.name: descent
returns.description: The descent of the Font in pixels.

getBaseline.description:
Gets the baseline of the Font.

Most scripts share the notion of a baseline: an imaginary horizontal line on which characters rest. In some scripts, parts of glyphs lie below the baseline.

returns.name: baseline
returns.description: The baseline of the Font in pixels.

params.name: text
params.description: A UTF-8 encoded unicode string.

returns.name: hasglyph
returns.description: Whether the font can render all the UTF-8 characters in the string.

getKerning.description:
Gets the kerning between two characters in the Font.

Kerning is normally handled automatically in love.graphics.print, Text objects, Font:getWidth, Font:getWrap, etc. This function is useful when stitching text together manually.

params.name: leftchar
params.description: The left character.

params.name: rightchar
params.description: The right character.

returns.name: kerning
returns.description: The kerning amount to add to the spacing between the two characters. May be negative.

setFallbacks.description: Sets the fallback fonts. When the Font doesn't contain a glyph, it will substitute the glyph from the next subsequent fallback Fonts. This is akin to setting a 'font stack' in Cascading Style Sheets (CSS).

params.name: fallbackfont1
params.description: The first fallback Font to use.

getDPIScale.description:
Gets the DPI scale factor of the Font.

The DPI scale factor represents relative pixel density. A DPI scale factor of 2 means the font's glyphs have twice the pixel density in each dimension (4 times as many pixels in the same area) compared to a font with a DPI scale factor of 1.

The font size of TrueType fonts is scaled internally by the font's specified DPI scale factor. By default, LÖVE uses the screen's DPI scale factor when creating TrueType fonts.

returns.name: dpiscale
returns.description: The DPI scale factor of the Font.

Drawable.description: Superclass for all things that can be drawn on screen. This is an abstract type that can't be created directly.

Mesh.description: A 2D polygon mesh used for drawing arbitrary textured shapes.

setVertices.description: Replaces a range of vertices in the Mesh with new ones. The total number of vertices in a Mesh cannot be changed after it has been created. This is often more efficient than calling Mesh:setVertex in a loop.

params.name: vertices
params.description: The table filled with vertex information tables for each vertex, in the form of {vertex, ...} where each vertex is a table in the form of {attributecomponent, ...}.

params.name: startvertex
params.description: The index of the first vertex to replace.

params.name: count
params.description: Amount of vertices to replace.

setVertex.description:
Sets the properties of a vertex in the Mesh.

In versions prior to 11.0, color and byte component values were within the range of 0 to 255 instead of 0 to 1.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the the vertex you want to modify (one-based).

params.name: attributecomponent
params.description: The first component of the first vertex attribute in the specified vertex.

getVertex.description:
Gets the properties of a vertex in the Mesh.

In versions prior to 11.0, color and byte component values were within the range of 0 to 255 instead of 0 to 1.

params.name: index
params.description: The one-based index of the vertex you want to retrieve the information for.

returns.name: attributecomponent
returns.description: The first component of the first vertex attribute in the specified vertex.

setVertexAttribute.description:
Sets the properties of a specific attribute within a vertex in the Mesh.

Meshes without a custom vertex format specified in love.graphics.newMesh have position as their first attribute, texture coordinates as their second attribute, and color as their third attribute.

params.name: vertexindex
params.description: The index of the the vertex to be modified (one-based).

params.name: attributeindex
params.description: The index of the attribute within the vertex to be modified (one-based).

params.name: value1
params.description: The new value for the first component of the attribute.

params.name: value2
params.description: The new value for the second component of the attribute.

getVertexAttribute.description:
Gets the properties of a specific attribute within a vertex in the Mesh.

Meshes without a custom vertex format specified in love.graphics.newMesh have position as their first attribute, texture coordinates as their second attribute, and color as their third attribute.

params.name: vertexindex
params.description: The index of the the vertex you want to retrieve the attribute for (one-based).

params.name: attributeindex
params.description: The index of the attribute within the vertex to be retrieved (one-based).

returns.name: value1
returns.description: The value of the first component of the attribute.

returns.name: value2
returns.description: The value of the second component of the attribute.

getVertexCount.description: Gets the total number of vertices in the Mesh.

returns.name: count
returns.description: The total number of vertices in the mesh.

getVertexFormat.description: Gets the vertex format that the Mesh was created with.

returns.name: format
returns.description: The vertex format of the Mesh, which is a table containing tables for each vertex attribute the Mesh was created with, in the form of {attribute, ...}.

setAttributeEnabled.description: Enables or disables a specific vertex attribute in the Mesh. Vertex data from disabled attributes is not used when drawing the Mesh.

params.name: name
params.description: The name of the vertex attribute to enable or disable.

params.name: enable
params.description: Whether the vertex attribute is used when drawing this Mesh.

isAttributeEnabled.description: Gets whether a specific vertex attribute in the Mesh is enabled. Vertex data from disabled attributes is not used when drawing the Mesh.

params.name: name
params.description: The name of the vertex attribute to be checked.

returns.name: enabled
returns.description: Whether the vertex attribute is used when drawing this Mesh.

attachAttribute.description: Attaches a vertex attribute from a different Mesh onto this Mesh, for use when drawing. This can be used to share vertex attribute data between several different Meshes.

params.name: name
params.description: The name of the vertex attribute to attach.

params.name: mesh
params.description: The Mesh to get the vertex attribute from.

detachAttribute.description: Removes a previously attached vertex attribute from this Mesh.

params.name: name
params.description: The name of the attached vertex attribute to detach.

returns.name: success
returns.description: Whether the attribute was successfully detached.

flush.description:
Immediately sends all modified vertex data in the Mesh to the graphics card.

Normally it isn't necessary to call this method as love.graphics.draw(mesh, ...) will do it automatically if needed, but explicitly using **Mesh:flush** gives more control over when the work happens.

If this method is used, it generally shouldn't be called more than once (at most) between love.graphics.draw(mesh, ...) calls.

setVertexMap.description:
Sets the vertex map for the Mesh. The vertex map describes the order in which the vertices are used when the Mesh is drawn. The vertices, vertex map, and mesh draw mode work together to determine what exactly is displayed on the screen.

The vertex map allows you to re-order or reuse vertices when drawing without changing the actual vertex parameters or duplicating vertices. It is especially useful when combined with different Mesh Draw Modes.

params.name: map
params.description: A table containing a list of vertex indices to use when drawing. Values must be in the range of Mesh:getVertexCount().

getVertexMap.description:
Gets the vertex map for the Mesh. The vertex map describes the order in which the vertices are used when the Mesh is drawn. The vertices, vertex map, and mesh draw mode work together to determine what exactly is displayed on the screen.

If no vertex map has been set previously via Mesh:setVertexMap, then this function will return nil in LÖVE 0.10.0+, or an empty table in 0.9.2 and older.

returns.name: map
returns.description: A table containing the list of vertex indices used when drawing.

setTexture.description: Sets the texture (Image or Canvas) used when drawing the Mesh.

params.name: texture
params.description: The Image or Canvas to texture the Mesh with when drawing.

getTexture.description: Gets the texture (Image or Canvas) used when drawing the Mesh.

returns.name: texture
returns.description: The Image or Canvas to texture the Mesh with when drawing, or nil if none is set.

setDrawMode.description: Sets the mode used when drawing the Mesh.

params.name: mode
params.description: The mode to use when drawing the Mesh.

getDrawMode.description: Gets the mode used when drawing the Mesh.

returns.name: mode
returns.description: The mode used when drawing the Mesh.

setDrawRange.description: Restricts the drawn vertices of the Mesh to a subset of the total.

params.name: start
params.description: The index of the first vertex to use when drawing, or the index of the first value in the vertex map to use if one is set for this Mesh.

params.name: count
params.description: The number of vertices to use when drawing, or number of values in the vertex map to use if one is set for this Mesh.

getDrawRange.description: Gets the range of vertices used when drawing the Mesh.

returns.name: min
returns.description: The index of the first vertex used when drawing, or the index of the first value in the vertex map used if one is set for this Mesh.

returns.name: max
returns.description: The index of the last vertex used when drawing, or the index of the last value in the vertex map used if one is set for this Mesh.

ParticleSystem.description:
A ParticleSystem can be used to create particle effects like fire or smoke.

The particle system has to be created using update it in the update callback to see any changes in the particles emitted.

The particle system won't create any particles unless you call setParticleLifetime and setEmissionRate.

clone.description: Creates an identical copy of the ParticleSystem in the stopped state.

returns.name: particlesystem
returns.description: The new identical copy of this ParticleSystem.

setTexture.description: Sets the texture (Image or Canvas) to be used for the particles.

params.name: texture
params.description: An Image or Canvas to use for the particles.

getTexture.description: Gets the texture (Image or Canvas) used for the particles.

returns.name: texture
returns.description: The Image or Canvas used for the particles.

setBufferSize.description: Sets the size of the buffer (the max allowed amount of particles in the system).

params.name: size
params.description: The buffer size.

getBufferSize.description: Gets the maximum number of particles the ParticleSystem can have at once.

returns.name: size
returns.description: The maximum number of particles.

setInsertMode.description: Sets the mode to use when the ParticleSystem adds new particles.

params.name: mode
params.description: The mode to use when the ParticleSystem adds new particles.

getInsertMode.description: Gets the mode used when the ParticleSystem adds new particles.

returns.name: mode
returns.description: The mode used when the ParticleSystem adds new particles.

setEmissionRate.description: Sets the amount of particles emitted per second.

params.name: rate
params.description: The amount of particles per second.

getEmissionRate.description: Gets the amount of particles emitted per second.

returns.name: rate
returns.description: The amount of particles per second.

setEmitterLifetime.description: Sets how long the particle system should emit particles (if -1 then it emits particles forever).

params.name: life
params.description: The lifetime of the emitter (in seconds).

getEmitterLifetime.description: Gets how long the particle system will emit particles (if -1 then it emits particles forever).

returns.name: life
returns.description: The lifetime of the emitter (in seconds).

setParticleLifetime.description: Sets the lifetime of the particles.

params.name: min
params.description: The minimum life of the particles (in seconds).

params.name: max
params.description: The maximum life of the particles (in seconds).

getParticleLifetime.description: Gets the lifetime of the particles.

returns.name: min
returns.description: The minimum life of the particles (in seconds).

returns.name: max
returns.description: The maximum life of the particles (in seconds).

setPosition.description: Sets the position of the emitter.

params.name: x
params.description: Position along x-axis.

params.name: y
params.description: Position along y-axis.

getPosition.description: Gets the position of the emitter.

returns.name: x
returns.description: Position along x-axis.

returns.name: y
returns.description: Position along y-axis.

moveTo.description: Moves the position of the emitter. This results in smoother particle spawning behaviour than if ParticleSystem:setPosition is used every frame.

params.name: x
params.description: Position along x-axis.

params.name: y
params.description: Position along y-axis.

setEmissionArea.description: Sets area-based spawn parameters for the particles. Newly created particles will spawn in an area around the emitter based on the parameters to this function.

params.name: distribution
params.description: The type of distribution for new particles.

params.name: dx
params.description: The maximum spawn distance from the emitter along the x-axis for uniform distribution, or the standard deviation along the x-axis for normal distribution.

params.name: dy
params.description: The maximum spawn distance from the emitter along the y-axis for uniform distribution, or the standard deviation along the y-axis for normal distribution.

params.name: angle
params.description: The angle in radians of the emission area.

params.name: directionRelativeToCenter
params.description: True if newly spawned particles will be oriented relative to the center of the emission area, false otherwise.

getEmissionArea.description: Gets the area-based spawn parameters for the particles.

returns.name: distribution
returns.description: The type of distribution for new particles.

returns.name: dx
returns.description: The maximum spawn distance from the emitter along the x-axis for uniform distribution, or the standard deviation along the x-axis for normal distribution.

returns.name: dy
returns.description: The maximum spawn distance from the emitter along the y-axis for uniform distribution, or the standard deviation along the y-axis for normal distribution.

returns.name: angle
returns.description: The angle in radians of the emission area.

returns.name: directionRelativeToCenter
returns.description: True if newly spawned particles will be oriented relative to the center of the emission area, false otherwise.

setDirection.description: Sets the direction the particles will be emitted in.

params.name: direction
params.description: The direction of the particles (in radians).

getDirection.description: Gets the direction of the particle emitter (in radians).

returns.name: direction
returns.description: The direction of the emitter (radians).

setSpread.description: Sets the amount of spread for the system.

params.name: spread
params.description: The amount of spread (radians).

getSpread.description: Gets the amount of directional spread of the particle emitter (in radians).

returns.name: spread
returns.description: The spread of the emitter (radians).

setSpeed.description: Sets the speed of the particles.

params.name: min
params.description: The minimum linear speed of the particles.

params.name: max
params.description: The maximum linear speed of the particles.

getSpeed.description: Gets the speed of the particles.

returns.name: min
returns.description: The minimum linear speed of the particles.

returns.name: max
returns.description: The maximum linear speed of the particles.

setLinearAcceleration.description:
Sets the linear acceleration (acceleration along the x and y axes) for particles.

Every particle created will accelerate along the x and y axes between xmin,ymin and xmax,ymax.

params.name: xmin
params.description: The minimum acceleration along the x axis.

params.name: ymin
params.description: The minimum acceleration along the y axis.

params.name: xmax
params.description: The maximum acceleration along the x axis.

params.name: ymax
params.description: The maximum acceleration along the y axis.

getLinearAcceleration.description:
Gets the linear acceleration (acceleration along the x and y axes) for particles.

Every particle created will accelerate along the x and y axes between xmin,ymin and xmax,ymax.

returns.name: xmin
returns.description: The minimum acceleration along the x axis.

returns.name: ymin
returns.description: The minimum acceleration along the y axis.

returns.name: xmax
returns.description: The maximum acceleration along the x axis.

returns.name: ymax
returns.description: The maximum acceleration along the y axis.

setRadialAcceleration.description: Set the radial acceleration (away from the emitter).

params.name: min
params.description: The minimum acceleration.

params.name: max
params.description: The maximum acceleration.

getRadialAcceleration.description: Gets the radial acceleration (away from the emitter).

returns.name: min
returns.description: The minimum acceleration.

returns.name: max
returns.description: The maximum acceleration.

setTangentialAcceleration.description: Sets the tangential acceleration (acceleration perpendicular to the particle's direction).

params.name: min
params.description: The minimum acceleration.

params.name: max
params.description: The maximum acceleration.

getTangentialAcceleration.description: Gets the tangential acceleration (acceleration perpendicular to the particle's direction).

returns.name: min
returns.description: The minimum acceleration.

returns.name: max
returns.description: The maximum acceleration.

setLinearDamping.description: Sets the amount of linear damping (constant deceleration) for particles.

params.name: min
params.description: The minimum amount of linear damping applied to particles.

params.name: max
params.description: The maximum amount of linear damping applied to particles.

getLinearDamping.description: Gets the amount of linear damping (constant deceleration) for particles.

returns.name: min
returns.description: The minimum amount of linear damping applied to particles.

returns.name: max
returns.description: The maximum amount of linear damping applied to particles.

setSizes.description:
Sets a series of sizes by which to scale a particle sprite. 1.0 is normal size. The particle system will interpolate between each size evenly over the particle's lifetime.

At least one size must be specified. A maximum of eight may be used.

params.name: size1
params.description: The first size.

params.name: size2
params.description: The second size.

params.name: size8
params.description: The eighth size.

getSizes.description: Gets the series of sizes by which the sprite is scaled. 1.0 is normal size. The particle system will interpolate between each size evenly over the particle's lifetime.

returns.name: size1
returns.description: The first size.

returns.name: size2
returns.description: The second size.

returns.name: size8
returns.description: The eighth size.

setSizeVariation.description: Sets the amount of size variation (0 meaning no variation and 1 meaning full variation between start and end).

params.name: variation
params.description: The amount of variation (0 meaning no variation and 1 meaning full variation between start and end).

getSizeVariation.description: Gets the amount of size variation (0 meaning no variation and 1 meaning full variation between start and end).

returns.name: variation
returns.description: The amount of variation (0 meaning no variation and 1 meaning full variation between start and end).

setRotation.description: Sets the rotation of the image upon particle creation (in radians).

params.name: min
params.description: The minimum initial angle (radians).

params.name: max
params.description: The maximum initial angle (radians).

getRotation.description: Gets the rotation of the image upon particle creation (in radians).

returns.name: min
returns.description: The minimum initial angle (radians).

returns.name: max
returns.description: The maximum initial angle (radians).

setSpin.description: Sets the spin of the sprite.

params.name: min
params.description: The minimum spin (radians per second).

params.name: max
params.description: The maximum spin (radians per second).

getSpin.description: Gets the spin of the sprite.

returns.name: min
returns.description: The minimum spin (radians per second).

returns.name: max
returns.description: The maximum spin (radians per second).

returns.name: variation
returns.description: The degree of variation (0 meaning no variation and 1 meaning full variation between start and end).

setSpinVariation.description: Sets the amount of spin variation (0 meaning no variation and 1 meaning full variation between start and end).

params.name: variation
